findings.consequence: Pallet jams at the conveyor entry will not be detected. The conveyor motor will continue running and pushing pallets against obstructions, risking mechanical damage to battery packs, pallet tooling, conveyor belts, and motor drive assemblies.
findings.evidence: Cause-and-effect matrix entry CE-ST10-03 and narrative §3 require that if the conveyor entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) remains blocked for more than 5.0 s while the conveyor motor M-1001 (Y10) is running, the conveyor must stop and a latched jam alarm must be raised. The parameter table defines T10 with a preset of 5.0 s (jam_time), and lint confirms X11 is in the I/O list but never referenced. R2 resets M190 (LD X1 / RST M190) and R3 evaluates M190 to de-energize Y10, but the logic to monitor X11, time T10, and latch M190 is entirely missing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add jam detection and latch rungs before R2: drive timer T10 (K50 for 5.0 s at 100 ms base) when Y10 is running and entry eye X11 is blocked (LD Y10, AND X11, OUT T10 K50). When T10 is done, latch the alarm using SET M190 (LD T10, SET M190).
findings.title: Missing conveyor entry jam detection logic (PE-1002 / T10 / M190)

findings.consequence: The conveyor can restart automatically without warning when a tripped motor overload cools down, exposing technicians inspecting the conveyor to crushing/entanglement hazards and repeatedly cycling a faulted motor into thermal breakdown.
findings.evidence: In R1, LDI X13 drives non-retentive coil OUT M191. When motor overload MOL-1001 trips (X13 opens to 0 V), M191 activates M199 in R3 and stops conveyor contactor Y10 in R4. However, because M191 is driven by OUT, if the thermal overload relay cools down or auto-resets, X13 returns to 24 V, causing M191 and M199 to de-energize immediately. Because selector switch SS-0003 (X2) is a maintained auto-mode contact, Y10 will immediately restart without operator intervention. Furthermore, R2 only resets M190 and does not reset M191.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the overload trip in R1 using SET M191 (LDI X13, SET M191). In R2, add RST M191 alongside RST M190 so that fault reset pushbutton PB-0002 (X1) must be pressed to clear the overload alarm once X13 is healthy.
findings.title: Unlatched conveyor motor overload alarm causing unexpected automatic restart hazard

findings.consequence: If RQ-1005 is received when no pallet is present, the stopper drops and incoming pallets will overshoot the test position. If released when the conveyor is stopped or during an E-stop, the pallet will not exit; after 2.0 s, the stopper will extend back up against the underside of the battery pack/pallet, causing physical damage or jamming. Actuating the stopper during an E-stop also violates safety isolation.
findings.evidence: In R6, LDP X14 directly executes SET Y11 without verifying Auto mode (X2), E-stop healthy (X0), pallet presence at the stop (X10 / M100), or that the conveyor motor is running (Y10). Furthermore, R8 only resets Y11 upon expiration of timer T11; Y11 is not reset if an E-stop occurs or if a station fault is triggered while Y11 is energized.
findings.proposed_fix: Add permissive interlocks to R6: LDP X14, AND X2, AND X0, AND X10, AND Y10, SET Y11. In addition, add an unconditional reset rung for Y11 if E-stop is lost or ST10 faults: LDI X0, OR M199, RST Y11.
findings.title: Missing operational permissives and E-stop reset on stopper release solenoid (Y11)

data.summary: Engineering review of the ST10 conveyor program identified three significant defects: (1) completely missing jam detection logic (PE-1002 / X11 and timer T10 never set jam alarm M190, violating cause-effect CE-ST10-03); (2) unlatched motor overload alarm M191 allowing the conveyor to restart automatically upon overload cooldown when Auto mode selector X2 is active; and (3) missing operational and safety permissives on stopper release solenoid Y11, which allows the stopper to actuate without a pallet present, during manual mode, or during an active E-stop.
